what_it_does: Serverless computing (also called Functions-as-a-Service, or FaaS) lets developers run code in the cloud without managing servers — the cloud provider spins up a container (a lightweight isolated execution environment) for each request and shuts it down afterward. The first time a function runs after being idle (a 'cold start'), it must import Python packages and load modules before it can do any useful work, and for machine-learning functions this initialization accounts for more than half the total cost. lambda-trim automatically reduces this overhead by figuring out which parts of each imported package a function actually uses, measuring how much each module costs in both time and money (cloud bills charge for both memory used and time elapsed), and then removing unused code paths before deployment. The optimized function is a drop-in replacement on any standard serverless platform — no changes to the cloud infrastructure needed.
